His father, William Irving (whose ancestry has been traced by genealogical enthusiasts to De Irwyn, armor-bearer to Robert Bruce), was a native of Shapinsha, one of the Orkney Islands; his mother, Sarah (Sanders) Irving, came from Falmouth.

arxiv-2012-10751.title: Total yield of electron-positron pairs produced from vacuum in strong electromagnetic fields: validity of the locally constant field approximation
arxiv-2012-10751.creator: D. G. Sevostyanov, I. A. Aleksandrov, G. Plunien, V. M. Shabaev
arxiv-2012-10751.description: Abstract The widely-used locally constant field approximation (LCFA) can be utilized in order to derive a simple closed-form expression for the total number of particles produced in the presence of a strong electromagnetic field of a general spatio-temporal configuration. A usual justification for this approximate approach is the requirement that the external field vary slowly in space and time.

arxiv-2206-02740.title: Transitivity and the existence of horseshoes on the 2 2 -torus Thanks: The first author was supported by CAPES - Finance code 001. The second author was partially supported by CNPq and FAPESP
arxiv-2206-02740.creator: Pollyanna Vicente Nunes, Fábio Armando Tal
arxiv-2206-02740.description: Abstract . We study the relationship between transitivity and topological chaos for homeomorphisms of the two torus. We show that if a transitive homeomorphism of 𝕋 2 \mathbb{T}^{2} is homotopic to the identity and has both a fixed point and a periodic point which is not fixed, then it has a topological horseshoe.

arxiv-2303-11429.title: Machine learning-based detection of cardiovascular disease using ECG signals: performance vs. complexity
arxiv-2303-11429.creator: Huy PHAM, Konstantin EGOROV, Alexey KAZAKOV, Semen BUDENNYY*
arxiv-2303-11429.description: Abstract Cardiovascular disease remains a significant problem in modern society. Among non-invasive techniques, the electrocardiogram (ECG) is one of the most reliable methods for detecting abnormalities in cardiac activities. However, ECG interpretation requires expert knowledge and it is time-consuming. Developing a novel method to detect the disease early could prevent death and complication.

arxiv-2305-06395.title: ACTC: Active Threshold Calibration for Cold-Start Knowledge Graph Completion
arxiv-2305-06395.creator: Anastasiia Sedova, Benjamin Roth
arxiv-2305-06395.description: Abstract Self-supervised knowledge-graph completion (KGC) relies on estimating a scoring model over (entity, relation, entity)-tuples, for example, by embedding an initial knowledge graph. Prediction quality can be improved by calibrating the scoring model, typically by adjusting the prediction thresholds using manually annotated examples.

arxiv-2410-04464.description: Abstract . In recent years, both degenerate versions and probabilistic extensions of many special numbers and polynomials have been explored. For instance, degenerate Bernstein polynomials and probabilistic Bernstein polynomials were investigated earlier. Assume that Y Y is a random variable whose moment generating function exists in a neighborhood of the origin.

arxiv-2501-16749.title: Topology optimization for microchannel heat sinks with nanofluids using an Eulerian-Eulerian approach
arxiv-2501-16749.creator: Chih-Hsiang Chen, Kentaro Yaji
arxiv-2501-16749.description: Abstract The demand for high-performance heat sinks has significantly increased with advancements in computing power and the miniaturization of electronic devices. Among the promising solutions, nanofluids have attracted considerable attention due to their superior thermal conductivity. However, designing a flow field that effectively utilizes nanofluids remains a significant challenge due to the complex interactions between fluid and nanoparticles.

arxiv-2505-00513.title: Group class operations and homological conditions
arxiv-2505-00513.creator: Ioannis Emmanouil and Wei Ren
arxiv-2505-00513.description: Abstract . Kropholler’s operation 𝐋𝐇 {\scriptstyle{{\bf LH}}} and Talelli’s operation Φ \Phi can be often used to formally enlarge the class of available examples of groups that satisfy certain homological conditions. In this paper, we employ this enlargement technique regarding two specific homological conditions.

arxiv-2505-14938.title: Scan, Materialize, Simulate: A Generalizable Framework for Physically Grounded Robot Planning
arxiv-2505-14938.creator: Amine Elhafsi, Daniel Morton, Marco Pavone
arxiv-2505-14938.description: Abstract Autonomous robots must reason about the physical consequences of their actions to operate effectively in unstructured, real-world environments. We present Scan, Materialize, Simulate (SMS), a unified framework that combines 3D Gaussian Splatting for accurate scene reconstruction, visual foundation models for semantic segmentation, vision-language models for material property inference, and physics simulation for reliable prediction of action outcomes.

arxiv-2512-04724.title: Crystal formation in systems of pseudo-forced swarmalators
arxiv-2512-04724.creator: Brennan J. H. Hughes, Christoph Bruder, Tobias Kehrer
arxiv-2512-04724.description: Abstract Swarmalators are active agents that move in position space and exhibit internal degrees of freedom. Due to interactions of their positions and phases of oscillation, they show on the one hand swarming, similar to the effect of flocking of birds. In addition, they exhibit synchronization behavior, analogous to what has been observed in fireflies.

pmc-10575132.title: A Novel Bird Sound Recognition Method Based on Multifeature Fusion and a Transformer Encoder
pmc-10575132.creator: Shaokai Zhang, Yuan Gao, Jianmin Cai, Hangxiao Yang, Qijun Zhao, Fan Pan, Loris Nanni
pmc-10575132.description: Birds play a vital role in the study of ecosystems and biodiversity. Accurate bird identification helps monitor biodiversity, understand the functions of ecosystems, and develop effective conservation strategies. However, previous bird sound recognition methods often relied on single features and overlooked the spatial information associated with these features, leading to low accuracy.

pmc-11305024.title: Sociodemographic determinants of HPV vaccine awareness, uptake, and intention among parents of adolescents in France 2021-22
pmc-11305024.creator: Alexia F Rivera, Josée M Dussault, Damien Oudin Doglioni, Sandra Chyderiotis, Jonathan Sicsic, Anne-Sophie Barret, Jocelyn Raude, Aurélie Gauchet, Amandine Gagneux-Brunon, Sébastien Bruel, Morgane Michel, Anne-Sophie Le Duc-Banaszuk, Nathalie Thilly, Judith E Mueller
pmc-11305024.description: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine coverage was <50% in France in 2022 and even lower among socially disadvantaged populations. We aimed to evaluate socio-demographic determinants of HPV vaccine awareness, uptake, and intention among parents of adolescents, and related attitudes and knowledge items.

pmc-11320021.title: Trityl isocyanide as a general reagent for visible light mediated photoredox-catalyzed cyanations†
pmc-11320021.creator: Irene Quirós, María Martín, Carla Pérez-Sánchez, Thomas Rigotti, Mariola Tortosa
pmc-11320021.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). A photoredox catalytic strategy has been developed to enable the functionalization of a variety of commercially available, structurally different radical precursors by the use of a bench-stable isonitrile as an efficient cyanating reagent. Specifically, a radical-based reaction has provided a mild and convenient procedure for the cyanation of primary, secondary and tertiary radicals derived from widely accessible sp3-hybridized carboxylic acids, alcohols and halides under visible light irradiation.

pmc-13361789.title: Frequency and Indications of Non-Musculoskeletal Examinations: A Cross-Sectional Survey of South African Chiropractors
pmc-13361789.creator: Zanéll Blignaut, Christopher Yelverton
pmc-13361789.description: Highlights What are the main findings? South African chiropractors routinely perform basic vital sign assessments (blood pressure and heart rate) and neurological examinations, but pulmonary, cardiac, abdominal, breast, and genitourinary examinations are conducted infrequently, with the majority of respondents reporting they never perform these assessments.Years of clinical experience did not influence examination frequency.

pmc-13369378.title: Sex- and Population-Specific Formulas for Glenoid Height–Based Assessment of Glenoid Bone Loss: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
pmc-13369378.creator: Woo-Sung Do, Tae-Hwan Yoon, Joon-Ryul Lim, Yun-Rak Choi, Yong-Min Chun
pmc-13369378.description: Background:Assessment of glenoid bone loss is essential in managing anterior shoulder instability. Although glenoid height–based methods are straightforward and practical for estimating native glenoid width in injured shoulders, inconsistent formulas across studies have created uncertainty in clinical practice, possibly due to population differences.

pmc-13648134.title: Association between shift work patterns and the incidence of prediabetes and diabetes among night shift workers: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13648134.creator: Hyundong Lee, Changil Shin, Minsun Kang, Jae Bum Park, Inchul Jeong, Jaehyuk Jung
pmc-13648134.description: BackgroundPrediabetes and diabetes represent major public health challenges, and shift work has been identified as a significant occupational risk factor. While two-shift systems are gaining preference over conventional three-shift systems, evidence comparing their risks for diabetes and prediabetes remains limited. We aimed to evaluate the risk of developing prediabetes and diabetes according to shift work patterns among night shift workers.

pmc-13677446.title: Valid Inference for Two Sample Summary Statistics Mendelian Randomization
pmc-13677446.creator: Kai Wang, Grace Z. Wang
pmc-13677446.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Mendelian randomization (MR) studies increasingly rely on summary statistics from genome‐wide association studies (GWASs). However, current summary‐data methods treat marginal GWAS effect estimates as independent across instrumental single‐nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), which holds only when the SNPs have no effect. Without imposing this independence assumption, we derive expressions for the two‐stage least squares (TSLS), two‐sample TSLS (TSTSLS), and generalized method‐of‐moments estimators together with their variance estimators using only GWAS summary statistics, assuming the instrumental SNPs are in linkage equilibrium.
